result.description: Manage source-owned resources, including skills, commands, context, docs, and scripts. Register sources, select resources for coding agents, attach docs to projects, and run declared scripts. Human output is the default; pass --json for the version 1 machine envelope. Append --help to any command path for its flags and examples.

flags.description: Print the version 1 JSON envelope; only status, sync, doctor, upgrade and version have a stable payload
flags.name: json

flags.description: Print the running Tack version; combines only with --json and --state-dir
flags.name: version

subcommands.description: Check the health of this machine's Tack: the release, state, built-in skill delivery, adapters, sources, projects, managed links and attached docs. Read-only, machine-wide, works before init and never fetches; each problem names the exact next command, and any failed check exits 1
subcommands.name: doctor

subcommands.description: List a project's attached docs resources and settings; attach source-owned docs, mount them in worktrees, search and serve them, and resolve writing targets. Bare `docs`, `docs list` and `docs ls` list. The project is --project, or the registered project containing --cwd or the current directory.
subcommands.name: docs

subcommands.description: Run trusted scripts declared by registered sources; `catalog --kind script` lists them
subcommands.name: script

subcommands.description: Inspect and clear retained script run history
subcommands.name: history

subcommands.description: Initialize Tack state; safe to repeat
subcommands.name: init

subcommands.description: Inspect registered sources and their health; register and relocate them. Bare `source`, `source list` and `source ls` inspect
subcommands.name: source

subcommands.description: Resolve the resources declared by every registered source, with the issues that kept candidates or sources out; --kind narrows it to one resource kind
subcommands.name: catalog

subcommands.description: Browse the catalog and edit one destination in an interactive terminal; refuses unless stdin and stdout are interactive
subcommands.name: explore

subcommands.description: Inspect every registered project, its roots and its health, whatever the current directory; register and refresh Git projects. Bare `project`, `project list` and `project ls` inspect
subcommands.name: project

subcommands.description: Change exact include and exclude choices per project or user; `pick` lists them
subcommands.name: choice

subcommands.description: List persisted choices in every namespace, or only in --project or --user. Bare `pick`, `pick list` and `pick ls` list; choices are still changed with `pick include` and `pick remove`
subcommands.name: pick

subcommands.description: List the enabled coding-agent adapters, whatever the current directory; enable and disable the adapters that receive links. Bare `adapter`, `adapter list` and `adapter ls` list
subcommands.name: adapter

subcommands.description: Preview link changes that deliver the selected resources to enabled adapters; --apply writes them. Bare selects the containing project; --all selects every project and the user target.
subcommands.name: reconcile

subcommands.description: Preview reconciliation; the read-only alias of reconcile without --apply, with the same target rules
subcommands.name: plan

subcommands.description: Inspect source, project, selection, destination and pending-removal health. Bare selects the containing project; --all selects every project and the user target.
subcommands.name: status

subcommands.description: Preview removing the managed links of the selected target; --apply removes them. Bare selects the containing project; --all selects every project and the user target.
subcommands.name: clean

subcommands.description: Preview retrying pending removals; --apply retries them. Bare selects the containing project; --all selects every project and the user target.
subcommands.name: retry

subcommands.description: Preview removing every managed link and all Tack state; --apply deletes state only after cleanup settles
subcommands.name: reset

subcommands.description: Update and roll back the installed Tack release, and optionally schedule the update; `upgrade status` reads it. Updating is a deterministic command with no agent or model involved
subcommands.name: self

subcommands.description: Read the installed Tack release without fetching or writing anything. Release changes are still `upgrade`, `upgrade rollback` and `upgrade schedule`
subcommands.name: upgrade
